title: A required note must be filled in to submit, and is listed as outstanding
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a user with "Settings - Service" enabled, on the build under test.
  2. A template with a checkbox field that has "Note required if Monitor / Not OK" on, and a per-axle field with it on (seed via Settings - Service > Inspection Templates > Add field, turn the option on, Save).
  3. You are filling an inspection against that template: open a work order, start the inspection, with "Work order lines - Create & Edit" enabled.
custom_steps:
1. On the checkbox field, select Monitor or Not OK, leave the note empty, and try to Submit.
  2. Before submitting, open the outstanding-items list and look for the field.
  3. On the per-axle field, set a single position to Not OK and check whether a note is required.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • With the option on, choosing Monitor or Not OK requires a note before the inspection can be submitted.
  • The requirement is enforced at Submit, not only while filling the form.
  • Before submit, the field appears in the outstanding-items list, so the technician is not rejected by an avoidable error.
  • On a per-axle field the note requirement is driven by the verdicts on the positions, not a stored axle roll-up; a single Not OK position requires the note as soon as it is set, and the requirement triggers when any axle is marked Monitor or Not OK.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9099 (S1 — Require a note on flagged responses); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S1; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R3: “When the option is on and the technician selects Monitor or Not OK, a note will be required before the inspection can be submitted”
  • S1-R4: “The system will enforce the requirement on submit, not only while the technician is filling the form”
  • S1-R5: “Before submit, the technician will see the field listed among the outstanding items, so they are not rejected by an error they could have avoided”
  • S1-R7: “On a per-axle field the requirement is triggered by the verdicts recorded on the positions, not by an axle's stored roll-up. A single Not OK tire will require the note as soon as it is set”

title: Note required: what it does not apply to, and unusual cases
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a user with "Settings - Service" enabled, on the build under test.
  2. Templates with the note option on and off, plus a template created before this release; you are filling inspections against them (seed the templates in Settings - Service > Inspection Templates).
custom_steps:
1. With the option off, mark Monitor / Not OK with no note and Submit.
  2. Mark OK or N/A and Submit.
  3. Enter a note of only spaces on a flagged field.
  4. Write a note then change the response to OK.
  5. Open a pre-release template, then turn the option on mid-inspection.
  6. On an unlabelled field, read its outstanding-items row; and on a per-axle field with all positions OK but a stale flagged roll-up, check whether a note is required.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • With the option off, a Monitor or Not OK response with no note submits successfully.
  • An OK or N/A response never requires a note.
  • A note containing only spaces counts as empty.
  • Templates created before this release are unaffected until an author opens one and turns the option on.
  • Turning the option on while an inspection is already in progress leaves that inspection on the rule it started with.
  • A note written then abandoned (response changed to OK) is kept.
  • An unlabelled field is identified in the outstanding-items list by its type and position, not shown as an empty row.
  • A per-axle field whose positions all read OK requires no note, even if an axle carried a flagged roll-up from an earlier response shape.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9099 (S1 — Require a note on flagged responses); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S1; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-N1: “If the option is off, a Monitor or Not OK response with no note will submit successfully”
  • S1-N2: “If the response is OK or N/A, no note will be required”
  • S1-E1: “A note containing only spaces counts as empty”
  • S1-E2: “Templates created before this release are unaffected until an author opens one and turns the option on”
  • S1-E3: “If the option is turned on while an inspection is already in progress, that inspection keeps the rule it started with”
  • S1-E4: “If the technician writes a note and then changes the response to OK, the note is kept”
  • S1-E6: “If the field has no label, the outstanding-items list still identifies it by its type and position rather than showing an empty row”
  • S1-E7: “A per-axle field whose positions all read OK will not require a note, even if an axle carried a flagged roll-up from an earlier response shape”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.

  • A checkbox field's authoring options include an option, "Photo required if Not OK".
  • That option is off by default for a newly added checkbox field.
  • With the option on, choosing Not OK requires at least one photo before the inspection can be submitted, enforced at Submit (not only while filling).
  • Before submit, the field appears in the outstanding-items list.
  • The option applies to checkbox fields only; a per-axle field records a verdict per position, with no single position a field photo would belong to.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9440 (S17 — Require a photo on a Not OK response); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S17; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S17-R1: “A checkbox field will offer an authoring option, "Photo required if Not OK"”
  • S17-R2: “The option will be off by default for newly added checkbox fields, starters included”
  • S17-R3: “When the option is on and the technician selects Not OK, at least one photo will be required before the inspection can be submitted”
  • S17-R4: “The system will enforce the requirement on submit, not only while the technician is filling the form”
  • S17-R5: “Before submit, the technician will see the field listed among the outstanding items, so they are not rejected by an error they could have avoided”
  • S17-R6: “The option applies to checkbox fields only. A per-axle field records a verdict per position, and there is no single position a photo of the field would belong to”

Amended on 3 October 2026
S17-R2 changed from on to off by default: Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905 (last modified 29 September 2026, read on 2 October 2026), and Jira SV-9440 updated to match. The S17-R2 quote above is the current wording. Because a new checkbox field no longer has the option on, the precondition now says the template's checkbox field has it turned on, so the Not OK steps still test the rule. The build last checked, v26.36.8-2a64085, still defaults the option on; story defect SV-10789 is open, so the automated E2E check for this expectation (submission-rules-photo.spec.ts, C88510) fails until it is fixed.

title: Choose which work order gets the lines, or a new one, before drafting
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', on the build under test; ShopCoach is enabled and the shop has at least one labor type.
  2. A completed inspection with at least one Monitor or Not OK finding, run on a work order. Seed it:
  3. ↳ Open a work order for a customer and asset (Work Orders > New, pick the customer/unit).
  4. ↳ Start an inspection from a template that has a checkbox field; mark one field Not OK and one Monitor.
  5. ↳ Complete and sign the inspection so it is in its read-only completed view.
  6. ↳ For eligibility: have one inspection whose run-on work order is Estimate/Approved/In Progress/Review, and one whose work order is Complete/Invoiced/Paid/Declined (or already invoiced).
custom_steps:
1. Open the completed inspection and press the build action; read the destination menu before any drafting starts.
2. On the eligible-work-order inspection, confirm the run-on work order is offered (by number and status).
3. On the ineligible-work-order inspection, confirm a new work order is created without asking, for the same customer and asset.
4. Confirm an ineligible destination keeps its place in the menu and states why.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Building lines requires ShopCoach; without it the completed inspection offers only the report and a link to its work order, and no build action.
  • The target is chosen before any drafting starts: the work order the inspection was run on, or a new work order.
  • The run-on work order is offered only while it is an eligible build target (status Estimate, Approved, In Progress or Review).
  • When the run-on work order is not eligible (Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, or an invoice already exists), a new work order is created without asking.
  • A new work order is created for the same customer and asset as the run-on work order, using their current values.
  • The destination is chosen from a menu on the build action itself, listing this work order (by number and status) and a new one seeded with the customer and unit, each going straight to drafting.
  • A destination that cannot take lines keeps its place in the menu and says why, rather than silently disappearing.
  • The build action looks the same everywhere: ShopCoach purple with the AI badge, labelled Build lines, with a chevron where it opens the destination menu.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9100 (S2 — Turn findings into work order lines); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S2; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R0: “Building lines requires ShopCoach. Without it the completed inspection offers the report and a link to its work order, and no build action at all”
  • S2-R3: “The user will choose the target before any drafting starts: the work order the inspection was run on, or a new work order”
  • S2-R4: “The system will offer the work order the inspection was run on only while that work order is an eligible build target. Eligible means Estimate, Approved, In Progress or Review. This document does not describe a work order as open or closed: the platform carries several competing definitions of open, and this rule names its own predicate rather than joining them”
  • S2-R5: “When the work order the inspection was run on is not an eligible build target, the system will create a new work order without asking. It is ineligible when its status is Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, or when an invoice already exists. Declined counts as ineligible because lines added to a refused order would revive work the customer turned down”
  • S2-R6: “A new work order will be created for the same customer and asset as the work order the inspection was run on, using their current values”
  • S2-R14: “The destination will be chosen from a menu on the build action itself rather than from a dialog raised before it. The menu lists this work order — by number and status — and a new one seeded with the customer and unit. Either target goes straight to the drafting”
  • S2-R15: “A destination that cannot take lines will keep its place in the menu and say why. A destination that silently stops being offered reads as a fault”
  • S2-R16: “The build action will have one appearance wherever it is met — the ShopCoach purple with the AI badge, labelled Build lines, with a chevron where it opens the destination menu”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.

title: A line built from an inspection behaves like any approved line
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', on the build under test; ShopCoach is enabled and the shop has at least one labor type.
  2. A completed inspection with at least one Monitor or Not OK finding, run on a work order. Seed it:
  3. ↳ Open a work order for a customer and asset (Work Orders > New, pick the customer/unit).
  4. ↳ Start an inspection from a template that has a checkbox field; mark one field Not OK and one Monitor.
  5. ↳ Complete and sign the inspection so it is in its read-only completed view.
  6. ↳ Note the shop's "automatically approve work order lines" setting and its default labor type (Settings - Service).
custom_steps:
1. Build the lines and open the target work order's Lines tab.
2. Check each Monitor/Not OK finding produced at least one line, and that a line is indistinguishable from a typed one.
3. Check the line's approval state against the shop setting, its labor type/rate, and the carried time estimate (editable; zero if none proposed).
4. Confirm the line did not arrive as a Fixed Line Total line.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Every Monitor and Not OK finding is represented by at least one line, with ShopCoach composing each line's name, description, time estimate and parts from the finding.
  • A generated line then behaves as an ordinary work order line, indistinguishable from one a user typed.
  • Added lines arrive approved or awaiting authorisation according to the shop's setting for automatically approving lines, exactly as a manually added line does.
  • A work order already in Approved status does not need re-approval, because approval applies to lines rather than to the work order.
  • A generated line takes the shop's default labor type (or the first available if no default is set), and the labor rate follows from the labor type.
  • ShopCoach's proposed time estimate is carried onto the line and is editable before adding; where none is proposed the line arrives at zero.
  • A generated line never arrives as a Fixed Line Total line; it is an ordinary labor-and-parts line, and switching it to a fixed total stays a deliberate act afterwards.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9100 (S2 — Turn findings into work order lines); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S2; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R1: “Every Monitor and Not OK finding will be represented by at least one line. ShopCoach composes each line's name, description, time estimate and parts; the field label, the measured value and the technician's note are inputs to that drafting rather than the line text itself (S15)”
  • S2-R2: “A generated line will behave as an ordinary work order line from that point on, indistinguishable from one a user typed”
  • S2-R7: “When the lines are added, they will arrive approved or awaiting authorisation according to the shop's existing setting for automatically approving work order lines, exactly as a manually added line does”
  • S2-R8: “A work order in Approved status will not require re-approval, because approval applies to lines rather than to the work order”
  • S2-R9: “A generated line will take the shop's default labor type, and where no default is set, the first labor type available to the shop. The labor rate will follow from the labor type. This is stated as a rule of its own rather than as a reference to the manual New Line form, whose fallback is behaviour of that form and not of the server”
  • S2-R10: “The time estimate ShopCoach proposes will be carried onto the line, and will be editable before the line is added. Where no estimate is proposed the line arrives at zero, to be estimated by whoever plans the work”
  • S2-R18: “A generated line never arrives as a Fixed Line Total line. It is an ordinary labor-and-parts line, and switching it to a fixed total stays a deliberate act afterwards. A fixed total requires labor plus parts to equal it exactly or the line cannot be saved, and a drafted line arrives carrying both figures”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.

title: Build lines is not offered until the inspection is ready for it
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', on the build under test; ShopCoach is enabled and the shop has at least one labor type.
  2. Seed three states: (a) an inspection that is not completed; (b) a completed inspection with only OK/N/A findings (no Monitor or Not OK); (c) a shop configured with no labor types.
custom_steps:
1. On the not-completed inspection, confirm the build is not offered.
2. On the completed inspection with only OK/N/A findings, confirm the build is not offered.
3. On a shop with no labor types, confirm the build does not run and states the reason.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • If the inspection is not completed, the build is not offered.
  • If the inspection has no Monitor or Not OK findings, the build is not offered.
  • If the shop has no labor types, the build does not run and states the reason, because a line cannot be created without a labor type or a fixed price.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9100 (S2 — Turn findings into work order lines); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S2; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-N1: “If the inspection is not completed, the build will not be offered”
  • S2-N2: “If the inspection has no Monitor or Not OK findings, the build will not be offered”
  • S2-N6: “If the shop has no labor types, the build will not run. A work order line cannot be created without a labor type or a fixed price, and S2-R18 forbids a generated line from being a Fixed Line Total, so the action states the reason rather than producing a line that cannot be saved”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.

title: Building lines with long notes, many findings, or a deleted work order
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', on the build under test; ShopCoach is enabled and the shop has at least one labor type.
  2. Two completed inspections to build from: one with a very long technician note, one with about thirty Monitor or Not OK findings (seed via a template with ~30 checkbox fields all marked Not OK).
  3. A second browser (or private window) signed in as another user who can close, delete or reopen the work order or the inspection.
custom_steps:
1. Build from the long-note inspection and check the drafted line reflects the whole note (nothing cut off).
2. Build from the thirty-finding inspection and check there is no cap and no extra confirmation, and that every finding is drafted (a set too large to draft at once is split across runs, not dropped).
3. Start a build choosing 'add to the open work order', then in the second browser close or delete that work order before you confirm; check the result matches the expected result below.
4. Repeat, using the second browser to reopen the inspection, and to delete the built lines versus delete the work order; check each result against the expected result below.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A very long note is given to ShopCoach whole, rather than truncated before it is read.
  • An inspection with thirty flagged findings builds without a cap or extra confirmation; a run too large to draft at once is split rather than the surplus dropped.
  • If the chosen open work order was closed by someone else in the meantime, the system tells the user and creates nothing.
  • If the run-on work order is deleted before the user confirms, the build fails without creating a partial result.
  • If two users draft from the same inspection at once, the drafting itself duplicates nothing; duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable.
  • If the inspection is reopened by someone else while a draft is on screen, the draft stays usable and any lines already added are kept.
  • If the lines were built onto a new work order and that work order is later deleted, the inspection counts as needing a work order again, while the inspection itself is unaffected.
  • Reversing an invoice does not change the inspection's state, because the work order and its lines still exist.
  • If the lines built from an inspection are deleted while the work order remains, the inspection stays actioned and does not return to needing a work order.
  • If the run-on work order is deleted, the inspection survives it and stays listed on the asset with a dash in its work order column; any lines added to that work order are gone with it and the inspection counts as needing a work order again.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9100 (S2 — Turn findings into work order lines); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S2; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-E2: “If a note is very long, it is given to ShopCoach whole rather than truncated before it is read”
  • S2-E3: “An inspection with thirty flagged findings is built without a cap and without an extra confirmation. If the assistant cannot draft that many in one run, the run is split rather than the surplus findings being dropped (S15-R14)”
  • S2-E4: “If the user chose to add lines to the open work order and it was closed by someone else in the meantime, the system tells the user and creates nothing”
  • S2-E5: “If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted before the user confirms, the build fails without creating a partial result”
  • S2-E6: “If two users draft from the same inspection at once, nothing is duplicated by the drafting itself, because a draft is not a work order line. Duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable”
  • S2-E7: “If the inspection is reopened by someone else while a draft is on screen, the draft stays usable and any lines already added are kept”
  • S2-E9: “If the lines were built onto a new work order and that work order is later deleted, the inspection counts as needing a work order again. The inspection itself is unaffected, because it belongs to the work order it was run on”
  • S2-E10: “Reversing an invoice does not change the inspection's state, because the work order and its lines still exist”
  • S2-E11: “If the lines built from an inspection are deleted while the work order remains, the inspection stays actioned and does not return to needing a work order. Deleting a work order is usually a correction; deleting a line is somebody who read the proposed work and decided against it, and re-raising the flag would ask them to do it again”
  • S2-E12: “If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted, the inspection survives it (S5-R21) and stays listed on the asset with a dash in its work order column. Where the lines had been added to that same work order they are gone with it, and the inspection counts as needing a work order again”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.

title: The summary card, counts per verdict, and the section review
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', on the build under test; ShopCoach is enabled and the shop has at least one labor type.
  2. A completed inspection with a mix of OK, Monitor and Not OK findings, and at least one verdict with no findings (seed a template with several checkbox fields and set the mix). Test both with ShopCoach enabled and with it disabled.

1. Read the summary card: completion line, a count per verdict, and the findings list naming each flagged position as field, axle, row and position with its reading.
2. Confirm a verdict with no findings is not counted on the card.
3. With ShopCoach, read the footer (View PDF, Go to work order, Build lines) and the one product note above it; without ShopCoach, read the footer (View PDF, Go to work order) and the plain line about the report, note feed and work order.

custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The screen leads with a summary card: the completion line, a count per verdict, and a findings list naming each flagged position (field, axle, row, position) with the reading that earned it.
  • A verdict with no findings under it is not counted on the card.
  • With ShopCoach the card footer offers View PDF, Go to work order and Build lines with the product named once above it; without ShopCoach it offers View PDF and Go to work order plus a plain line pointing to the customer report, the work order note feed and where the lines are added.
  • The section-by-section review sits below the summary card, and the service advisor, start time and per-section progress are not shown on this screen.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9101 (S3 — Build from a completed inspection); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S3; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R4: “The screen will lead with a summary card: the completion line, a count per verdict, and a findings list naming each flagged position as field, axle, row and position with the reading that earned it”
  • S3-R5: “A verdict with no findings under it will not be counted on the card. A zero reads as a finding at a glance, which is the opposite of what it says”
  • S3-R6: “With ShopCoach the card's footer will offer View PDF, Go to work order and Build lines, and a note above it will name the product once. Without ShopCoach the footer will offer View PDF and Go to work order, and the same space will carry a plain line saying the findings are on the customer report and in the work order note feed and that the lines are added on the work order”
  • S3-R7: “The section-by-section review of what the technician entered will stay below the summary card. The card answers what happened; the sections answer what was entered. The service advisor, the inspection's start time and per-section progress are not carried onto this screen: the first two belong to the work order the inspection was run on, and progress means nothing once the inspection is locked”

Expected results

  • The completed read-only view shows each field's verdict. A per-axle field shows each position's value and verdict and the axle's verdict; a measurement row has no verdict of its own.
  • The phone shows the same as the desktop, and the report follows S13-R0.
  • Counting is per axle — an axle contributes one count carrying the worst verdict of its positions — and the inspection list, the report counters and the field's own summary report the same numbers.
  • The one exception is the per-axle field's header on the fill screen, which counts flagged positions for the technician (for example '2 positions Not OK · 1 Monitor') and names no unit.

  • The finding names every flagged position on the row with its reading.

A count answers how many things need attention; a finding says what each one is. The one exception is the per-axle field's header on the fill screen, which counts flagged positions for the technician, for example '2 positions Not OK · 1 Monitor'. It names no unit, because a row knows its scope but not whether it measures a tire or a brake”

The completed view shows no verdict per measurement row and the phone matches the desktop; the per-axle field's header on the fill screen counts flagged positions; the finding names every flagged position with its reading. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”

title: At Risk count, its twelve-month trend line and the remembered window
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
  2. You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  3. You are in a location (workplace) with at-risk customers.
  4. In that location's At Risk table (Dashboard > View details on At Risk Customers) there are two customers whose invoices are inside the last twelve months: Customer A with Lifetime Invoices 1 and a parts-only invoice (e.g. Revenue (12 Mo) $40.50), and Customer B with Lifetime Invoices 2 or more. You have written down both names and the At Risk headline.

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 3: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: the At Risk Customers tile shows a number above 0. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
  • For 4: read the table's Lifetime Invoices and Revenue (12 Mo) columns; to see whether an invoice has only parts: Customers > the customer > Invoices tab (turn Open only off). Invoices cannot be back-dated, so if no such customers exist, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no such customers exist.
custom_steps:
1. Count the points on the At Risk trend line and compare its last point with the headline.
  2. On Customer A's invoice (Customers > Customer A > its work order > Finance tab > invoice three-dot menu > Issue Credit), credit every part on it and submit.
  3. Reload the dashboard and read the At Risk headline. Look for Customer A in the table.
  4. Credit every part on Customer B's latest invoice the same way.
  5. Reload the dashboard and look for Customer B in the table.
  6. Change the window pill to 60 days.
  7. Close the browser tab, open the site again in the same browser and open the dashboard.
  8. Click Dashboard in the top menu in a private window.
  9. Change your computer's time zone to one several hours away (computer settings > Date & Time), reload the dashboard and read the At Risk headline. Then set the time zone back.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The trend line has twelve points, one per month over the last twelve months. Its last point sits at the same level as the headline. Exact point values cannot be read off the trend line by hand: write 'point values not read' in the result comment.
  • After Customer A's twelve-month revenue drops to $0.00 (one lifetime invoice, no revenue above $0.00), Customer A is no longer at risk. The headline goes down by 1 and they leave the table.
  • Customer B stays in the table after their twelve-month revenue drops to $0.00, because they still have two or more lifetime invoices.
  • Back in the same browser, the pill still reads 60 days (remembered). In the private window it reads 120 Days (the default), because the choice is kept only in the browser where it was made.
  • Changing the computer's time zone does not change the At Risk headline: days are counted in the shop's own time zone.
  • That the count changes at the shop's own midnight cannot be checked by hand; write 'midnight change not checked by hand' in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9577 (Story 5, Count Tiles, Sales by Customer and At Risk Customers); story SV-9578 (Story 6, Expanding a Tile); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 5 and Story 6 (S6-R16). Design canvas boards 09_AtRisk_Window and 09_AtRisk_After (row 9).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R13: “The At Risk Customers sparkline shows the at-risk count over the trailing twelve months as twelve monthly points. Each historical point is the at-risk count as of the last day of that month in the workplace's timezone, using the inactivity window the tile currently shows. The twelfth point is computed as of now, rather than as of a month end that has not happened yet, so it always equals the headline. Every point is recomputed from current data, so a later void changes the past points: recording the count as it stood at the time would contradict S3-E2, which excludes a voided invoice even when deciding a customer's most recent invoice.”
  • S5-R14: “The inactivity window the user chose is remembered and applied on their next visit, in place of the 120-day default (S5-R11), under the storage rule in S6-R16.”
  • S5-R15: “Two parts of the at-risk definition are fixed here so the count cannot be read two ways. "Some revenue in the last twelve months" means revenue greater than $0.00 over the trailing twelve months, measured the way the Revenue tile measures revenue: invoice subtotals before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. A customer whose twelve-month revenue is exactly $0.00, or is negative because credits exceeded sales, does not satisfy this part of the test, though they can still qualify on the two-or-more-lifetime-invoices part. "At least the selected number of days old" is counted in whole calendar days in the selected workplace's timezone, from the date of the customer's most recent invoice to the current date. The count therefore changes at the shop's own midnight and is stable through the shop's working day, and two people viewing the same workplace from different places see the same number.”
  • Terminology (at-risk customer): “a customer who has bought before but whose most recent invoice is at least the selected number of days old (the inactivity window), and who also has either two or more lifetime invoices or some revenue in the last twelve months.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

  • S4-R11: “The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).”
  • S7-E1: “If the selected range has not finished, the tile's headline and sparkline both describe the same partial window.”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”

title: Core charge shows on the estimate and counts toward the totals
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user. That role holds every permission, including Part sales -> Create & Edit and Invoicing & payments -> Create & Edit.
  2. A test customer exists. If not: top menu Customers -> New Customer, enter a Name (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair") and click Save.
  3. A test vendor exists to order parts from. If not: top menu Parts -> Vendors (left sidebar) -> New Vendor, enter a Name (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Parts Supply"), pick a value in Taxes (required, e.g. "GST"), then click Save & Close.
  4. Start a new part sale today (a sale started before this release handles cores the old way): top menu Parts -> Part Sales -> New Part Sale; in the New part sale dialog pick the Customer and click Save. The sale opens with the status Estimate.
  5. On the Parts tab click Add Part (on a sale with no parts the Add Part dialog opens by itself). In the Add Part dialog enter Description "Water Pump", Quantity 1 (required), Vendor = the test vendor, Sell Price $517.55 and Core Charge $79.99, then click Save & Close. The grid shows the part and, beneath it, a row "Core for Water Pump".
  6. Leave the part unordered and unreceived: do not click Authorize or Order (on this build its Status column reads Requested).
  7. The sale's tax is GST at 5% (the expected figures use it; the Financial Info card names the tax, e.g. "GST"). If not, on the Financial Info card click the edit icon (tooltip "Edit tax rate"), pick "GST (5%)" in the Taxes list and click Save.
custom_steps:
1. Open the part sale you seeded and click the Finance tab.
  2. Set the Estimate / Invoice toggle to Estimate (the part is unreceived, so only the estimate exists).
  3. In the document's Parts section find the part row (with the example data: "Water Pump 1 $517.55 $517.55").
  4. Look directly beneath the part row for its core row, and read its label, indentation and amounts.
  5. In the Summary panel on the right, read the Parts, GST (5%) and Total figures.
  6. Confirm that at no point were you prompted to answer the core (no Ok / Not Ok question appeared).
  7. On the Finance tab click Create Invoice and note whether the sale can be invoiced while the part is still unreceived.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Beneath the part row a child row prints indented behind a ↳ arrow, labelled "Core charge", showing the core amount. With the example data it reads "↳ Core charge 1 $79.99 $79.99" directly under "Water Pump 1 $517.55 $517.55".
  • The core is counted in the totals: with the example data the Summary reads Parts $597.54, GST (5%) $29.88 and Total $627.42 (517.55 + 79.99 = 597.54; 597.54 x 5% = 29.88).
  • The "Core charge" child row is the same text size and weight as the part row above it, not the smaller greyer style of a fee or discount row.
  • No Ok / Not Ok prompt appears at any point - the core is charged automatically from the moment the part is quoted.
  • Create Invoice does not complete while the part is unreceived, so the pre-receipt core charge stays on the estimate and never reaches an invoice.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10262 (Story 1, Return a core on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 1; design canvas boards Cores_*/Document_*; read 5 Oct 2026 (specification edited that day). Source-verified 5 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R1: “A part sale charges its core to the customer from the moment the part is quoted. Nobody is asked anything. The estimate assumes the customer keeps the old unit until proven otherwise, so the charge is on the document before the part is received and stays on it after receipt”
  • S1-R13: “the core prints on the estimate as its own row directly beneath the part it belongs to, labeled Core charge, at the core charge amount, and it counts toward the parts total, the tax base and the sale total exactly as it does after receipt. A $517.55 part carrying a $79.99 core reads $517.55 then $79.99, and totals $597.54 of parts, $29.88 of GST at 5 percent and $627.42”
  • S1-R14: “The child rows keep a part row’s size and weight rather than an adjustment row’s ... a core charge is money in the total and reads like the part above it”
  • S1-N7: “A part sale offers no way to give that answer, so in practice every core on a part sale is charged until it is returned”
  • S1-N9: “A part sale can never reach an invoice while a part is still unreceived, so the pre-receipt core charge never leaves the estimate”

Last checked against build v26.40.7-7ffda69 on 10/5/2026.

custom_preconds:

  4. Sale A: top menu Parts -> Part Sales -> New Part Sale, pick the Customer and click Save; in the Add Part dialog enter "Water Pump" (Quantity 1, Vendor = the test vendor, Sell Price $517.55, Core Charge $79.99) and click Save & Add Part, then "Brake Pads" (Quantity 1, Sell Price $290.91) and click Save & Close. Then on the Finance tab click Add Deposit; in Create Deposit enter Deposit Amount $50.00 (e.g.) and a Payment Method (e.g. "Cash"), then click Record Deposit.
  5. Sale B: built exactly like Sale A, with its own $50.00 deposit.
  6. Sale C: a new part sale with one part ("Brake Pads", Quantity 1, $290.91, Vendor = the test vendor); click Authorize, then Order and Receive it (in the Receive parts dialog type a part number and Cost, then click Receive Parts), then on the Finance tab click Create Invoice. In the New Customer Payment dialog pick a Payment Method (e.g. "Cash") and click Make Payment for the full balance. (The payment dialog lists every open invoice for this customer and fills in an amount on each one: set the Payment amount of every other invoice to 0 so only this sale is paid.) Do not just close the dialog: closing it without paying cancels the invoice.
custom_steps:
1. On Sale A, tick the line with the core and use the menu ( ... ) above the parts list -> Split Part Sale (the new sale opens straight away); read where the deposit ends up.
  2. Confirm the selected line moves with its parts, returns and core to the new sale.
  3. On Sale B, tick every line and use the menu ( ... ) above the parts list -> Split Part Sale; read what the original Sale B keeps.
  4. On the original Sale B, reverse its held deposit (customer -> Deposits tab), then on the new sale use Add Deposit for the same amount (e.g. $50.00).
  5. On Sale C (invoiced), try to split it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The deposit stays with the original sale (a split does not move a deposit), as when a work order is split.
  • The split moves each selected line with its parts and returns, so a core and its charge travel with the line and are returned, if at all, on whichever sale the line lands on.
  • Moving every line is allowed; the original Sale B then keeps the deposit and no lines.

  • An already-invoiced sale cannot be split.

title: Permission matrix: what each role sees versus what the server enforces
custom_preconds:
1. Six test users exist on the build under test and you can sign in as each: (1) Owner/Admin; (2) View-only — Part Sales View without Create & Edit, e.g. the Office User role; (3) No-access — a Technician who cannot open part sales; (4) Parts-only — Part Sales Create & Edit but NOT Invoicing & Payments Create & Edit; (5) Vendor-perm — Vendor and order management only (this build has no permission named "Vendors"); (6) No-portal — no Customer Portal access.
  2. A part sale CREATED on this build exists, not invoiced, holding a received part with a core.
custom_steps:
1. As each user in turn, open the part sale (top menu Parts -> Part Sales -> click the sale; look at the parts list, the Financial Info card, the menu ( ... ) above the parts list and the Finance tab) and note whether these are OFFERED: Return Core, Cancel Return, Edit tax rate, Audit Log, Sales Representative, Add Deposit.
  2. As the View-only and Parts-only users, attempt each action by direct request (browser devtools re-send, or ask engineering to call the endpoint with that user's session).
  3. Record offered / hidden / server-refused per user per action.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Admin: all six offered and allowed.
  • View-only: none offered; every direct request refused by the server.
  • No-access: cannot open the part sale at all (See Financial Data gate).
  • Parts-only: Return Core, Cancel Return, Edit tax rate, Audit Log, Sales Representative offered; Add Deposit NOT offered and refused by the server (needs Invoicing & Payments Create & Edit).
  • Vendor-perm: Return Core and Cancel Return offered (shared core control); the part-sale-only actions are not.
  • The server enforces the WORK-ORDER edit permission for tax, rep and deposit: a user holding either Part Sales Create & Edit or Work Orders Create & Edit is allowed through.

title: Line text over 4,000 bytes is shortened from the end, title kept
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a service writer on the build under test, with a work order open.
  2. Seed and invoice a line whose joined text exceeds 4,000 bytes: a short title (e.g. "Replace tie rod"), a description, and a very long tech story.

  4. The shop has an active QuickBooks Online connection.
custom_steps:
1. To read the line text a customer/bookkeeper sees: open Export Reports, choose the Customer Invoice report and download it (requires "Invoicing & payments - View"); read the Description column.
  2. Read the long line's text: confirm the title (and as much that follows as fits) survives and the narrative is what gets clipped.
  3. Confirm no character is cut in half at the end.
  4. Compare where the plain line and the accented line are cut.
  5. Confirm the invoice reached QuickBooks and did not land in Unexported Items.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit and is never cut in the middle of a character; because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is clipped first (both the sync and the report cut at the same limit).
  • The limit is a storage (byte) limit, so an accented / non-Latin line may be shortened more than an English line that looks the same length; two equally-long-looking lines can be cut at different points - correct, not a defect.
  • A description long enough to be cut still syncs: the invoice reaches QuickBooks and does not land in Unexported Items.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667; story SV-10132 (S3, What Reaches QuickBooks); PRD (Confluence 845348896), Story 3; design board saved_resource(3); read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R7: “When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.”
  • S3-R7a: “The limit is a storage limit rather than a count of what a reader sees, so a line written with accented or non-Latin characters may be shortened more than an English line that looks the same length on screen. Two lines that look equally long can therefore be cut at different points. That is correct behavior and not a defect.”
  • S3-E3: “A description long enough to be cut still syncs. The invoice reaches QuickBooks; it does not land in Unexported Items.”

    • Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on and leave Min and Max empty.
    • In the Inventory section keep the bin row the dialog filled in ([Bin-1] = that bin, e.g. General Storage) and set its Quantity to 4.

  1. title: Bins of +5 and -2 show quantity 3 and $30 in Inventory Value
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user (Admin, also able to open Reports) · 1 browser · about 15 minutes
  • Build: the Part Lifecycle QA build (no build exists yet; use the build named in the test run).
  • User: you are signed in as an Admin, or as a user whose role has View, Create & Edit and Delete ticked in the Part Library and Inventory group of Settings → Roles & Permissions and who can see costs and prices.
  • Location: [Loc-1] = the location shown in the location switcher in the top bar when you start. Every part in this case is at [Loc-1].
  • Data: one part [Part-MIX] at [Loc-1] with two bins: [Bin-1] holding 5 and [Bin-2] holding -2 (net 3).
  • Every part here is tracked and costs $10.00 per unit. Negative bin quantities must be possible to enter by hand (see Setup).
  • Names, numbers and amounts marked (e.g. …) are examples; the quantities, costs, Min and Max values and the tracked or untracked state given here must hold exactly, because the expected results are worked out from them.

Setup

  1. Sign in, pick [Loc-1] in the location switcher in the top bar, and open Parts → Inventory (Active tab).
  2. Create [Part-MIX]: click New Inventory Part; type Description ZZAUTOTEST PL IV NET MIXED and Part Number ZZAUTOTEST-PL-IVNET-MIX-01; pick any Category (e.g. Uncategorized); type Cost 10.00.
    • Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on and leave Min and Max empty.
    • In the Inventory section keep the bin row the dialog filled in ([Bin-1] = that bin, e.g. General Storage) and set its Quantity to 5.
    • Click + Add Bin Location, pick another bin ([Bin-2] = that bin; if the list offers no other bin, first add one in Settings → Bin Locations, e.g. ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BIN-B) and set its Quantity to 0.
    • Click Save. The dialog closes.
  3. Write down [Part-MIX] = ZZAUTOTEST-PL-IVNET-MIX-01.
  4. Make [Bin-2] of [Part-MIX] hold -2: open [Part-MIX], in the Inventory section change the Quantity of [Bin-2] to -2, and click Save.
    • If the dialog does not accept a negative quantity, use Settings → Data Import → Inventory instead: download the template, fill one row for [Part-MIX] giving bin [Bin-2] the quantity -2, upload it and run the import.
    • If neither way accepts a negative quantity, stop here and mark this case Blocked with the comment "no way to create negative stock by hand".
  5. Check the setup worked: the [Part-MIX] row shows Bin Location / Quantity "[Bin-1] | 5" and "[Bin-2] | -2" and Average Cost $10.00.
custom_steps:
1. In the top bar click Reports and open the Inventory Value report.
  2. Leave the as-of date on today and set the Location filter to [Loc-1] only.
  3. Type ZZAUTOTEST-PL-IVNET-MIX- in the report's Search box.
  4. Read the rows listed (Qty, Unit Cost and Total Cost).
  5. Read the Totals row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: One row, [Part-MIX], with Qty 3.00, Unit Cost $10.00 and Total Cost $30.00 (5 + (−2) = 3; 3 × $10.00 = $30.00). It does not show Qty 5.00 or $50.00 (the positive bin alone).
  • Step 5: Totals reads Qty 3.00 and Total Cost $30.00.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
